question:
An engineer changed a configuration and must perform a rollback.
Which statement applies to a Cisco Nexus 5600 Series Switch?
options: The configuration rollback functionality is disabled when FCoE is enabled.
A system checkpoint is generated automatically when the running configuration is saved to NVRAM.
A user who is assigned to the network-operator user role is allowed to perform a rollback.
Errors are skipped when an atomic rollback type is triggered.
explanation:
Guidelines and Limitations -
Rollback has the following configuration guidelines and limitations:
- You can create up to ten checkpoint copies.
- You cannot apply the checkpoint file of one switch into another switch.
- Your checkpoint file names must be 75 characters or less.
- You cannot start a checkpoint filename with the word system.
- When FCoE is enabled, the checkpoint and configuration rollback functionality are disabled.
theory: NX-OS configuration rollback depends on the checkpoint/rollback infrastructure, which on Nexus 5600 platforms has documented interoperability limits with other features: specifically, when FCoE is enabled on the switch, the checkpoint and configuration rollback functionality is disabled altogether. This is a platform guideline rather than a role-based-access or automatic-checkpoint behavior, and it means an engineer planning a config rollback on that switch first needs to confirm FCoE isn't enabled. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 6 — Configuration Rollback, with Cisco documentation)
